_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
Every tool uses its own component, not GenericTool. The conversation at /c/{{SLUG}} ran the "tool smorgasbord": one call of nearly every tool. The page defines window.__toolEmoji(summary): the text of the ".tool-emoji" of the first ".tool" card that has a ".tool-command" matching summary (a string matches as a case-insensitive substring, a RegExp is tested against the whitespace-collapsed text), or "missing" if there is no such card. The transcript is taller than the screen and offscreen cards are content-visibility: auto, so check that cards exist (assert_count or eval) rather than that they are visible, unless a step says visible. Perform the steps in order.
1. Call "keyword_search": it must return exactly "absent" (the tool registry, GET /api/tools, has no keyword_search tool).
2. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}. Wait (allow 30s) until there are at least 15 [data-testid="tool-call-completed"] elements (an eval with expect). Then mount every card: dispatch a "beforeprint" Event on window (an eval without expect), and wait (allow 15s) until there is no ".tool-card-mount-placeholder" element (count 0).
3. There is no ".tool-status-icon" element (count 0).
4. "The bash card" is the first ".bash-tool" element whose text contains "echo 'hello from bash'". It exists, has a ".bash-tool-emoji" element inside, and its ".bash-tool-command" text contains "echo 'hello from bash'".
5. Thinking content appears inline, not as a tool card: the first ".thinking-content" element whose text contains "I'm thinking about the best approach" is visible, and an element inside it whose text contains "💭" is visible.
6. Diff, image and iframe tools keep their own card shapes: a ".patch-tool" element exists with a ".patch-tool-emoji" inside it.
7. A browser screenshot action renders the screenshot card: a ".screenshot-tool" element exists whose whitespace-collapsed text matches /\.png$|screenshot/i, and a ".screenshot-tool .screenshot-tool-emoji" element whose text contains "📷" exists. The read_image card is a ".screenshot-tool" element whose text contains "/tmp/image.png"; it has a ".screenshot-tool-emoji" inside whose text contains "🖼️". A browser screencast_stop renders a ".screencast-tool" element (one exists).
8. Each card renders its component's emoji. The browser families (emulate, network, accessibility, profile) are folded into the browser tool as <family>_<sub> actions, and the old standalone browser_* tool names still render the same components; the emoji proves the dispatch. In one eval, ['https://example.com', 'document.title', /^pdf$/, /console/i, '/tmp/test-prompt.txt', 'search "webhook backoff" author alice', /^device iphone_14$/, /^device ipad$/, /^enable$/, /^tree$/, /^metrics$/].map((s) => window.__toolEmoji(s)).join(' ') must equal exactly "🌐 ⚡ 📄 📋 🤖 🗄️ 📱 📱 📡 🌳 📊" (use that eval with this expect).
9. The browser pdf card links the saved file through /api/read: the first ".pdf-tool-link" element's href attribute (getAttribute) matches /^\/api\/read\?path=%2Ftmp%2Fshelley-pdfs%2F[0-9a-f-]+\.pdf$/ (an eval with expect "true"), and fetching that href from the page answers with the content-type header exactly "application/pdf" (an eval of fetch(href).then((r) => r.headers.get('content-type')) with that expect).
10. Summary lines carry no native title tooltip: there is no ".tool-command[title], .bash-tool-command[title]" element (count 0), and no ".tool-command:not(.change-dir-command) .ellipsis-start" element (count 0).
11. No tool falls back to GenericTool's gear: no ".tool-emoji" element whose text contains "⚙️" (assert_count 0 with that has_text).
